```{r load_data}

Elwha_data <- read.csv("cleaned_data.csv",check.names = T)

```

```{r str_data, echo=T}

str(Elwha_data)

```

```{r factor_dam}

Elwha_data$Dam_Condition <- as.factor(Elwha_data$Dam_Condition) 

#the dollar sign helps us give R an absolute reference, similar to Excel syntax 

```

```{r factor_site}
#your turn! change Site_Name to factor by replacing all instances of Dam_Condition with Site_Name, and then running the current chunk

#instructor note: you can replace terms manually, or you can use the find/replace feature in RStudio (magnifying glass icon). If using the find/replace option, you must select the text in the chunk and make sure to check "in selection" before replacing. Otherwise, you may inadvertently replace terms in the entire document.

Elwha_data$Site_Name <- as.factor(Elwha_data$Site_Name)

```

```{r str_check}

str(Elwha_data)

```

```{r preview_10}

Elwha_data[1:10,1:10] 

#lets us preview the first 10 rows and columns, respectively - [r,c], and the : between numbers means that you are looking at the continuous range between them, like what appears in Excel when you select consecutive cells. You could read it as “through,” so that 1:10 would read 1 through 10.

```

```{r preview_5}
#your turn! change the parameters to preview the first 5 rows and the first 5 columns instead of the first 10 rows and columns, and then running the current chunk

Elwha_data[1:5,1:5] 

```

```{r pH_mean}

mean_pH <- mean(Elwha_data$pH); mean_pH

```

```{r pH_val}

Elwha_data$pH

```

```{r pH_mean_na.rm}

mean_pH <- mean(Elwha_data$pH, na.rm = T); mean_pH

```

```{r pH_stats}
mean_pH <- mean(Elwha_data$pH, na.rm = T); mean_pH
median_pH <- median(Elwha_data$pH, na.rm = T); median_pH
min(Elwha_data$pH, na.rm = T)
max(Elwha_data$pH, na.rm = T)
sd_pH <- sd(Elwha_data$pH, na.rm = T); sd_pH

#note the use of a semi-colon to combine multiple commands to be more efficient

```

```{r temp_stats}
#your turn! calculate summary statistics for Temperature by replacing all instances of pH with Temperature, and then running the current chunk

#instructor note: you don't actually have to replace with "Temperature" in object names. You only need to replace pH with Temperature when it is a reference to a variable, e.g., preceded by $

mean_Temperature <- mean(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T); mean_Temperature
median_Temperature <- median(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T); median_Temperature
min(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T)
max(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T)
sd_Temperature <- sd(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T); sd_Temperature

#instructor note: this is an alternate version to demonstrate that pH doesn't need to be replaced with Temperature in all instances where pH appears, only where it is referencing the variable:

mean_temp <- mean(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T); mean_temp
median_temp <- median(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T); median_temp
min(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T)
max(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T)
sd_temp <- sd(Elwha_data$Temperature, na.rm = T); sd_temp


```

```{r DO_stats}
#your turn! calculate summary statistics for Dissolved_oxygen by replacing all instances of pH with Dissolved_oxygen, and then running the current chunk

mean_Dissolved_oxygen <- mean(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T); mean_Dissolved_oxygen
median_Dissolved_oxygen <- median(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T); median_Dissolved_oxygen
min(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T)
max(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T)
sd_Dissolved_oxygen <- sd(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T); sd_Dissolved_oxygen

#instructor note: this is an alternate version to demonstrate that pH doesn't need to be replaced with Dissolved_oxygen in all instances where pH appears, only where it is referencing the variable:

mean_DO <- mean(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T); mean_DO
median_DO <- median(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T); median_DO
min(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T)
max(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T)
sd_DO <- sd(Elwha_data$Dissolved_oxygen, na.rm = T); sd_DO

```

```{r t_test_pH}

pH.ttest <- t.test(pH~Dam_Condition, data=Elwha_data); pH.ttest

```

```{r t_test_temp}
#your turn! run a t-test for temp by replacing all instances of pH with Temperature, and then running the current chunk

Temperature.ttest <- t.test(Temperature~Dam_Condition, data=Elwha_data); Temperature.ttest

#instructor note: alternate version example

temp.ttest <- t.test(Temperature~Dam_Condition, data=Elwha_data); temp.ttest

```

```{r t_test_DO}
#your turn! run a t-test for Dissolved_oxygen by replacing all instances of pH with Dissolved_oxygen, and then running the current chunk

Dissolved_oxygen.ttest <- t.test(Dissolved_oxygen~Dam_Condition, data=Elwha_data); Dissolved_oxygen.ttest

#instructor note: alternate version example

DO.ttest <- t.test(Dissolved_oxygen~Dam_Condition, data=Elwha_data); DO.ttest

```

```{r during_subset}

during_dam <- subset(Elwha_data,Elwha_data$Dam_Condition=="During removal")
during_dam[1:5,1:5]

```

```{r pH_ANOVA}

pH_ANOVA <- aov(pH~Site_Name, data=during_dam)
summarypH <- summary(pH_ANOVA); summarypH

```

```{r DO_ANOVA}
#your turn! run an ANOVA comparing Dissolved_oxygen by replacing all instances of pH with Dissolved_oxygen, and then running the current chunk

Dissolved_oxygen_ANOVA <- aov(Dissolved_oxygen~Site_Name, data=during_dam)
summaryDissolved_oxygen <- summary(Dissolved_oxygen_ANOVA); summaryDissolved_oxygen

#instructor note: alternate version example
DO_ANOVA <- aov(Dissolved_oxygen~Site_Name, data=during_dam)
summaryDO <- summary(DO_ANOVA); summaryDO

```

```{r pH_boxplot}

plot(pH~Site_Name, data=during_dam, xlab="Sampling Site", ylab="pH")

```

```{r DO_boxplot}
#your turn! make a boxplot of dissolved oxygen by site after dam removal by replacing all instances of pH with Dissolved_oxygen, and then running the current chunk. For the ylab argument, you should name it "Dissolved oxygen (mg/L)" since we know the units.

plot(Dissolved_oxygen~Site_Name, data=during_dam, xlab="Sampling Site", ylab="Dissolved oxygen (mg/L)")

```

```{r load_libraries}
#run this chunk exactly as-is to install the packages and load the libraries contained in tidyverse

install.packages("tidyverse")
library(tidyverse)

```

```{r pH_dplyr}

pH_aov_plot <- during_dam %>% group_by(Site_Name) %>% summarize(mean=mean(pH,na.rm=T),sd=sd(pH,na.rm=T))

pH_aov_plot #object that contains all of the data we need to plot
  
```

```{r pH_barplot}

pH_plot <- ggplot(pH_aov_plot, aes(x=Site_Name, y=mean)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=Site_Name),stat="identity", color="black", position=position_dodge()) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd)) + labs(x="Sample Site",y="pH",fill="Sample Site")

pH_plot #displays the plot

```

```{r DO_barplot}
#your turn! make a barplot of dissolved oxygen by site after dam removal by replacing all instances of pH with Dissolved_oxygen, and then running the current chunk

Dissolved_oxygen_aov_plot <- during_dam %>% group_by(Site_Name) %>% summarize(mean=mean(Dissolved_oxygen,na.rm=T),sd=sd(Dissolved_oxygen,na.rm=T))

Dissolved_oxygen_aov_plot #object that contains all of the data we need to plot

Dissolved_oxygen_plot <- ggplot(Dissolved_oxygen_aov_plot, aes(x=Site_Name, y=mean)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=Site_Name),stat="identity", color="black", position=position_dodge()) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd)) + labs(x="Sample Site",y="Dissolved_oxygen  (mg/L)",fill="Sample Site")

Dissolved_oxygen_plot #displays the plot

#instructor note: alternate version example
DO_aov_plot <- during_dam %>% group_by(Site_Name) %>% summarize(mean=mean(Dissolved_oxygen,na.rm=T),sd=sd(Dissolved_oxygen,na.rm=T))

DO_aov_plot #object that contains all of the data we need to plot

DO_plot <- ggplot(DO_aov_plot, aes(x=Site_Name, y=mean)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=Site_Name),stat="identity", color="black", position=position_dodge()) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd)) + labs(x="Sample Site",y="Dissolved_oxygen (mg/L)",fill="Sample Site")

DO_plot #displays the plot

```

```{r temp_barplot}
#your turn! make a barplot of temperature by site after dam removal by replacing all instances of pH with Temperature, and then running the current chunk

Temperature_aov_plot <- during_dam %>% group_by(Site_Name) %>% summarize(mean=mean(Temperature,na.rm=T),sd=sd(Temperature,na.rm=T))

Temperature_aov_plot #object that contains all of the data we need to plot

Temperature_plot <- ggplot(Temperature_aov_plot, aes(x=Site_Name, y=mean)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=Site_Name),stat="identity", color="black", position=position_dodge()) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd)) + labs(x="Sample Site",y="Temperature (°C)",fill="Sample Site")

Temperature_plot #displays the plot

#instructor note: alternate version example
temp_aov_plot <- during_dam %>% group_by(Site_Name) %>% summarize(mean=mean(Temperature,na.rm=T),sd=sd(Temperature,na.rm=T))

temp_aov_plot #object that contains all of the data we need to plot

temp_plot <- ggplot(temp_aov_plot, aes(x=Site_Name, y=mean)) + geom_bar(aes(fill=Site_Name),stat="identity", color="black", position=position_dodge()) + geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sd, ymax=mean+sd)) + labs(x="Sample Site",y="Temperature (°C)",fill="Sample Site")

temp_plot #displays the plot

```

```{r ph_DO_scatter}

plot(Dissolved_oxygen~pH, data=Elwha_data,xlab="pH", ylab="Dissolved oxygen (mg/L)") #for units on Dissolved oxygen, we should check the metadata

```

```{r pH_DO_lm}
DO_pH_reg <- lm(Dissolved_oxygen~pH, data=Elwha_data)
summary(DO_pH_reg) #our results

plot(Dissolved_oxygen~pH, data=Elwha_data,xlab="pH", ylab="Dissolved oxygen (mg/L)") #for units on Dissolved oxygen, we should check the metadata
abline(DO_pH_reg) #plots our regression line

```

```{r temp_DO_scatter_lm}
#your turn! make a scatterplot of dissolved oxygen by temperature by replacing all instances of pH with Temperature, and then running the current chunk

DO_Temperature_reg <- lm(Dissolved_oxygen~Temperature, data=Elwha_data)
summary(DO_Temperature_reg) #our results

plot(Dissolved_oxygen~Temperature, data=Elwha_data,xlab="Temperature (°C)", ylab="Dissolved oxygen (mg/L)") #for units on Dissolved oxygen, we should check the metadata
abline(DO_Temperature_reg) #plots our regression line

#instructor note: alternate version example
DO_temp_reg <- lm(Dissolved_oxygen~Temperature, data=Elwha_data)
summary(DO_temp_reg) #our results

plot(Dissolved_oxygen~Temperature, data=Elwha_data,xlab="Temperature (°C)", ylab="Dissolved oxygen (mg/L)") #for units on Dissolved oxygen, we should check the metadata
abline(DO_temp_reg) #plots our regression line

```
